from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        bit0 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.5)

        bit1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.5)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The puzzle has rods and disks.", "Move disks without breaking the rules.", "Three disks require seven moves."]
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create disk assets
        disk_colors = [RED, GREEN, BLUE]
        disks = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.3, width=1.0 + i*0.5, color=disk_colors[i], fill_opacity=1) for i in range(3)])
        rod = Rectangle(height=2.0, width=0.2, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Group setup for animation
        # Starting Rod
        rod1 = rod.copy()
        stack1 = VGroup(*disks).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.0).next_to(rod1, DOWN, buff=-2.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        rod1_pos = self.place_in_area(VGroup(rod1, stack1), "A1", "F2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(rod1), Create(stack1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Moving smallest disk to target
        self.play(stack1[2].animate.shift(RIGHT * 3.0 + UP * 2.0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        # Moving middle disk
        self.play(stack1[1].animate.shift(RIGHT * 3.0 + UP * 1.5))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Sequence", [
            "Binary counter matches disk movement.",
            "Observe the rhythmic bit-flip pattern.",
            "Disks follow binary logic perfectly."
        ])
        
        # Reveal lecture lines
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture))

        # Create Tree structure
        tree = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, color="#7B68EE", fill_opacity=0.5),
            Circle(radius=0.3, color="#7B68EE", fill_opacity=0.5),
            Circle(radius=0.3, color="#7B68EE", fill_opacity=0.5)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        lines = VGroup(
            Line(tree[0].get_right(), tree[1].get_left()),
            Line(tree[1].get_right(), tree[2].get_left())
        )
        
        root = VGroup(tree, lines)
        self.place_in_area(root, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#7B68EE"), Create(tree))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), tree[1].animate.set_fill(opacity=1.0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(lines))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Conclusion", [
            "Binary is recursive algorithm DNA.", 
            "Complex puzzles hide simple logic.", 
            "Logic patterns are everywhere."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        summary_group = VGroup(
            Text("Binary DNA", color="#FFD700", font_size=32),

        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(summary_group, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        logic_label = Text("Simple Mapping", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(logic_label, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(logic_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.play(FadeOut(summary_group), FadeOut(logic_label))
        final_msg = Text("The End", color="#808080", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(final_msg, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(final_msg))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Binary Language
sections.content: Introduce binary (base-2) as a system using only 0 and 1. Use the visual of a light switch (Off=0, On=1) to explain how numbers are represented by place values (powers of 2).

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: 3 rods and n disks of different sizes. Rules: move one disk at a time, never place a larger disk on a smaller one. Goal: Move all disks to the target rod.
sections.example: A 3-disk stack. The minimum moves required is 2^n - 1. For 3 disks: 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to Binary
sections.content: Explain the elegant connection: The binary sequence of numbers from 1 to 2^n - 1 tells us exactly which disk to move at each step. If the number of the step is written in binary, the position of the rightmost '1' indicates the disk number (starting from 1).
sections.example: For 3 disks, step 3 is '011' in binary. The rightmost '1' is at the 1st position, meaning we move the smallest disk (Disk 1).

sections.title: Visualizing the Sequence
sections.content: Use a synchronized animation timeline. The left side shows the binary counter incrementing (001, 010, 011...), and the right side shows the physical movement of the disks on the rods.
sections.example: Show a robot arm moving Disk 1 on odd steps and the next available disk on even steps, following the binary 'bit-flip' pattern.

sections.title: Synthesis & Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize how binary is not just for computers but is the 'DNA' of recursive algorithms. Reiterate that complex puzzles are often just simplified logic patterns hidden in plain sight.
sections.example: A final visual: A clock-like device where the 'Binary Gears' automatically solve the Towers of Hanoi as the counter ticks forward.
